add-step: Add a new step to the current task based on conversation context
add-idea: Capture a deferred idea to the worklog Ideas section — quickly log anything worth revisiting without losing it mid-session
create-task: Create a task file from current discussion — lighter alternative to /start-feature
start: Confirm project readiness in one sentence
start-feature: Run a structured discovery interview before starting a new feature — explores the codebase, asks one question at a time, presents decision packages with options + recommendation, then creates a spec and task file
plan-tasks: Read an existing spec and propose a task breakdown — assesses separable work streams, proposes split, creates task files linked to the spec
load-task: Load task context, show progress, and surface ambiguities and conflicts before implementation
load-spec: Load a feature spec, its linked tasks, and feature-level progress and gaps
review-task: Validate the current task — plan quality, spec coverage, deliverable alignment, and context consistency
run-step: Execute one plan step; optional step number.
run-task: Run pending steps, then after_task finalization; does not close the task.
close-task: Close the task: update tracking and optionally its GitHub issue.
gh-resolve-pr: Fix CI and review findings on a GitHub PR, then report readiness.
align-context: Update all context files (task, spec, task-context, worklog) to reflect current state of work — fixes stale entries, fills missing knowledge, reports what changed
do-it: Turn the current discussion into a task step and implement it — adds step to task file, updates spec if needed, then implements with review-fix loop
challenge: Pause and push back — surface questions, wrong assumptions, concerns, and better alternatives before proceeding
brainstorm: Generate missing angles, better implementations, and new combinations — creative expansion that complements /challenge
thoughts: Quick honest take — share thoughts, concerns, or better ideas about the current discussion without a heavy audit
interview: Run a structured breadth-first interview to explore a topic thoroughly — walks dimensions, batches independent questions, recommends answers, captures decisions
commit: Commit current changes following project commit rules (template, body settings).
review: Review code changes for bugs, security, edge cases. Scope with args — diff (default), branch, commit, path. Reviews inline.
deep-review: Comprehensive code review — architecture + correctness. Scope with args — diff (default), branch, all, path. Reviews inline.
next-step: Mark previous step as done in the task file, then start the next step
draft-pr: Draft a pull request title and body to a local file — no push, no GitHub PR
make-pr: Push the current branch when needed and create a GitHub pull request from the local draft
gh-review-check: Check unresolved PR review comments and summarize findings
draft-issue: Draft a GitHub issue based on a discussion or requirements in the current conversation
generate-docs: Generate project documentation from code and AIContext artifacts — reference (internal technical), guide (user-facing), or both
prepare-release: Prepare a version release — follows project release config in `.aicontext/release.md`, runs first-time setup if config is missing
gh-review-fix-loop: Fix and resolve GitHub PR review threads.
gh-fix-tests: Fix failing GitHub CI checks on a PR.
web-inspect: Browser-based investigation using playwright-cli — open pages, inspect elements, check console errors, capture screenshots. Headed mode by default.
aic-help: Show AIContext quickstart guide with setup, workflows, and best practices
aic-skills: Show all available AIContext skills grouped by workflow stage
tidy-aic: Archive completed tasks, specs, and worklog entries — clean up .aicontext/ clutter
